newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover slumps in week to Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover slumps in week to Nov 15.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 40.6 percent slump in its weekly turnover and traders said activity fell on tightened liquidity resulting from an increased reserve requirement.

Total BSE turnover during the week ending November 15 dropped to 20.18 million dinars ($4 million) from 33.98 million dinars a week ago, while the number of deals fell to 149 from 172, the bourse said in its report.

"The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) decision to increase the reserve requirement to 15 from 10 percent as of November 11 weighed heavily on market liquidity," BSE spokesman Milko Stimac told Reuters.
Traders said the 15 percent reserve requirement caused further tightening of market liquidity. "There are no fresh funds and a large number of investors withdraw money," a trader said.
"Half of the investors withdraw funds purely out of devaluation fears, while the rest do so because they really need money," another trader said.
Banks, normally the most active market players, have been hit the hardest by the latest NBY measure, an analyst said.

"The NBY measure will drain some 450 million dinars from the banking sector. If the total capacity of the sector never exceeds 300 million dinars, you see what this measure means for the market," said the analyst who asked not to be named.
Tight liquidity has also reflected on an unofficial giro money market, where banks trade their surplus liquidity.
Total weekly turnover on the giro money market stood at 24.6 million dinars, down on 35.15 million dinars a week ago.
"Volume on this unofficial interbank market fell, and it will need time to absorb the harsh blow," the analyst said.
Interest rates on giro money deals ranged between a daily 0.4 and 0.5 percent, corresponding to 13.7 and 15 percent per month.
For the week ending November 15, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 76 percent of the total BSE turnover with 128 deals worth 15.86 million dinars.
*Treasury bills traded 19 times for a volume of 2.52 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 210 and 520 percent. Traders expected rates to resume an upward trend soon.
*The BSE reported only one deal in wheat selling forward contracts worth 1.608 million dinars.

*There was no trade in the NBY short-term bonds. Commercial banks, the only buyers of the bonds, have silently boycotted the bonds ever since the NBY launched the reserve requirement in September. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
